# JSON serialization issue with ipaddress classes as alternative

### Description

JSON serialization seems to have an issue when a value is typehinted with `ipaddress` classes as an alternative - interestingly this seems to depend on the order of declaration.

As the pasted code example shows, a value typehinted as `bool | ipaddress.IPv4Address` serializes differently from `ipaddress.IPv4Address | bool`. Note how the value is (incorrectly) converted to a `str` in the `BadModel` class.

### Example Code

```Python
import ipaddress

from pydantic import BaseModel


class GoodModel(BaseModel):
    value: bool | ipaddress.IPv4Address


class BadModel(BaseModel):
    value: ipaddress.IPv4Address | bool


# OKAY: {'value': True}
print(GoodModel(value=True).model_dump(mode="json"))

# ISSUE - value is str: {'value': 'True'} 
print(BadModel(value=True).model_dump(mode="json"))
```
